central_main_stem.description: The primary vertical axis of the plant. A thick, pale cream/white stem with visible node swellings at each branching point. Runs from the root mound at approximately y=820 up to the apex flower bud at y=105. The stem passes directly through the mid-page text zone and is the sole bisecting agent for all 10 loci. Its width at mid-page is approximately 30–40 normalized units, creating a consistent gap in all bisected lines.

apex_flower_bud.description: A closed tulip-like flower bud at the very apex of the central stem. Has a dark brown/black cap and pale white petals partially opening. Small in size relative to the leaf mass. Situated at the topmost point of the plant, well above the text zone.

upper_stem_node_1.description: The first branching node immediately below the apex bud. Bears two pairs of opposite leaves — one pair teal (green), one pair tan (ochre). Leaves are broad ovoid with smooth outlines. Thorn-like projections visible at node junction.

upper_stem_node_2.description: The second major branching node, bearing a denser cluster of leaves at a slightly lower position. Multiple teal and tan ovoid leaves radiate outward. More pronounced thorn projections visible. This node and its leaves define the upper-mid illustration zone.

mid_stem_node_left.description: Left lateral branch emerging from the main stem at approximately y=430. Bears 3–4 alternate leaves (mix of teal and tan ovoids) on a sub-branch angling lower-left. The lowest leaf of this branch descends into the upper text zone.

mid_stem_node_right.description: Right lateral branch emerging from the main stem at approximately y=410. Mirror of the left lateral branch, bearing 3–4 alternate leaves angling lower-right into the right text column zone.

lower_stem_node_left.description: The lowest visible left sub-branch, bearing 2 large leaves (one teal, one tan) that descend to approximately y=680, penetrating deeply into the upper text block zone. This branch and its leaves are the primary left-side illustration elements constraining left-column text width in the upper paragraph.

lower_stem_node_right.description: The lowest visible right sub-branch, bearing 2 large leaves that descend to approximately y=660. Constrains right-column text in the upper paragraph similarly to its left counterpart.

thorn_projections.description: Short pointed spine-like protrusions emerging from the stem at each node junction, rendered in the same pale cream ink as the stem. Botanically suggest a thorny or prickly shrub species. These are small features (~10–20 normalized units each) and do not independently affect text layout.

root_mound.description: A large bulging mound at the base of the central stem, drawn in tan/brown ink with a dense overlapping scale or pinecone-like texture. This is the most prominent root representation in the herbal section — suggesting a bulb or corm rather than spreading roots. It occupies most of the lower third of the page below the text blocks and is entirely text-free.

root_hair_fringe.description: Fine radiating root-hair lines drawn outward from the perimeter of the root mound in a grass or fringe pattern. They extend the root illustration to the very bottom edge of the parchment. Entirely below the text zone.
